plan: Plan track T15 (Bot complete) and ADR-043 (Bot: devices, pairing, control and safety); the computer plugin and the job worker serve OpenVibe.Actor and the Codes job runner (tracks T14/T17)
release: v0.25.0, published 2026-10-27 as a GitHub release (the egress guard: every connection every agent browser makes, a page's own scripts included, goes through a proxy the plugin runs on 127.0.0.1 that resolves, checks and connects to the address it checked, so a page never reaches the machine's own network below level full; browser_egress: open turns it off; v0.24.1: a kept profile carries session cookies too: Chrome drops cookies that end with the browser as it quits, and a sign-in is often one, so a desk keeps them beside the profile and the next desk's browser gets them back as it starts, found by the production proof; v0.24.0: kept desk profiles: desk start takes profile, so a desk's browser starts from the person's kept profile (sign in once, on any desk) and saves it back when it stops, closing the browser gracefully so its cookies are written, the last desk to stop wins, caches never kept, and each desk's own copy removed; the browser follows a page its page opens (a sign-in popup, a new tab) and comes back when it closes; the agent's clicks count as a person's, so sites open their sign-in popups; v0.23.0: browser desks, the Desks plan's step D2: desk start takes kind browser, a headless browser alone with no display at about half the cost of a whole desk, on Linux or macOS; its page is its screen, mouse and keyboard and live view over the browser's pipe, exactly the desk's size; a desk host, which has no screen or input of its own, gets screen, screen_stream and input on its desks; a click on a named desk scales to that desk's size; v0.22.0: desks on a desk host, found by the first production proof: a desk's temp folder is short (Chrome's SingletonSocket must fit a Unix socket path, and the desks folder on a desk host was too deep, so Chrome closed as it started), and a desk no command used for desk_idle_s (15 minutes) stops by itself, so a desk an agent left behind when it crashed or restarted ends; v0.21.0: element refs and receipts, the Desks plan's step D3: the agent's browser lists a page's interactive elements as compact refs (e7 button "Sign in"), kept on the element while it stays, and click, press and back answer with what changed (url, lines that appeared, lines gone), so agents act on the page's structure before screenshots; v0.20.0: desk hosts, the Desks plan's step D5: install.sh --desk-host turns an old laptop, a mini PC or a spare workstation into a host of desks for its owner's agents, run as its own openvibe-desk account with Xvfb, openbox, D-Bus, xdotool, ImageMagick and Chromium installed and max_desks sized to its memory; v0.19.0: several desks per machine, the Desks plan's step D1: the computer plugin runs named desks (desk-<name>, private kept), each with its own X display, D-Bus, browser profile, downloads and temp folder, up to max_desks (one per 2 GiB of memory by default), so two agents work at once without seeing or driving each other's screen; proven with two real Chrome desks that never share a cookie; v0.18.0: a motion command's validity also counts the time it waits in the queue to its plugin and in the pipe: the core fixes the instant it expires at receipt, writes what is left at the moment it writes the line with expires_at_mono_ns on the clock it shares with the plugin, and never writes one that has run out, and the Python runtime refuses one that ran out in the pipe before handle(); the clock bound is kept in nanoseconds and counts Bot's whole-millisecond stamps, rounded up from nanoseconds; a Node booting latched sets the e-stop on its plugins before starting them; the Python SDK package reports the Node release; v0.17.0: deadlines are checked against the latest the server's clock can be: the estimate plus its bound, the connection's fastest round trip, and motion waits for that bound on every new connection; every stop and estop names its cause, hello carries the newest halt epoch, and the Python SDK gives drivers on_stop(StopInfo) and on_resume to tell an ordinary stop from an emergency without re-arming anything; v0.16.1: the Python runtime refuses a motion command whose deadline passed while it waited behind a slow handler, so a driver never moves on a stale command; plugins.md answers where deadlines come from, re-stamping, order across a change of driver, stop versus estop, and that nothing is held past its validity; v0.16.0: openvibe-node quit ends a running node cleanly with nothing latched, for launchers; each driver command carries its provenance (link session, seq, Bot send time and deadline) and a halt's stop its turn_epoch, and the Python runtime refuses a replay on a session and a command from an ended turn; the no-redelivery contract written down in plugins.md): binaries for linux amd64/arm64/armv7, darwin amd64/arm64 and windows amd64, the plugins tarball, install.sh and SHA256SUMS
runtime: go 1.24 (one static binary per platform); plugins in Python 3; an ESP32 Arduino library
deployment: none of its own: people install it on their machines and robots (curl -fsSL https://openvibe.bot/install | sh, or a release binary); it connects out to OpenVibe.Bot (wss://openvibe.bot/device) and pairs through OpenVibe.Bot or OpenVibe.Network. On 2026-10-22 production held 1 platform node with 4 pairings and 5 node principals on Network, and 3 robots with 5 devices on Bot.
features: pairing with a code approved on openvibe.bot (or through Network), one outbound WebSocket, no open ports
safety: deadlines, owner limits clamped before any driver, heartbeats and a deadman, a persisted e-stop and the local kill switch (openvibe-node stop)

plugins as separate processes (JSON lines): dryrun, adeept_adr036, cozmo, relay and ros2 (rclpy or rosbridge); the community LOOI driver's contract; signed community profiles (openvibe-node profile verify)

the computer plugin for OpenVibe.Actor: terminal, files, screen, input and its own browser, at the level the owner sets on the machine (observe, ask, trusted, full); approvals in the tray (Linux, Windows), a notification or openvibe-node approve
the live screen: the machine's screen on openvibe.bot for its owner only, up to 30 minutes
the job worker (--worker): sandboxed function, code and linux jobs, and the OpenVibe.Codes job runner
one-command install on a Raspberry Pi or other Linux robot (I2C, SPI, camera tools, kit detection)
system service on systemd, launchd and Windows (or a Windows sign-in start)
ESP32 library (OpenVibeNode): pairing, control link, drive and actuator commands, telemetry, heartbeat, deadman and e-stop
notYet: code signing and notarization for Windows and macOS (the release has SHA256SUMS only)
a tray on macOS (approvals there are a dialog with Deny as its default)
the computer plugin's browser on Windows
